result.title: Bayesian Low-Rank Posteriors for Scalable Membership Inference
result.summary: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) aim to determine whether a sample was used during the training of a target model. Strong MIAs rely on reference (or shadow) models to estimate target-conditional score distributions, but training such ensembles is computationally expensive for modern large-scale Vision--Language Models (VLMs). In this work, we propose a scalable alternative that replaces explicit reference-model training with a Bayesian approximation over low-rank adaptation parameters. Specifically, we model uncertainty only within the LoRA subspace and construct a posterior from a single training run, from which we sample a diverse set of \emph{virtual reference models}. We instantiate this approach using Stochastic Weight Averaging Gaussian (SWAG), enabling efficient approximation of target-conditional score distributions at a fraction of the cost of conventional shadow-model ensembles. We evaluate the resulting attack on three downstream-adapted VLMs across two privacy-sensitive visual question answering tasks, namely Document VQA and Medical VQA. To isolate the effect of pretraining knowledge, we additionally introduce a controlled synthetic dataset. Our approach outperforms standard reference-based attacks while requiring only a single reference-model fine-tuning run, making membership inference more practical for large VLMs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向大规模 VLM 的成员推断攻击，用 LoRA 子空间上的贝叶斯低秩后验（SWAG）从单次训练中采样「虚拟参考模型」，替代昂贵的 shadow 模型集成来估计目标条件分数分布，并在 Document VQA 与 Medical VQA 等适配后 VLM 上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「单次训练即在低秩子空间内采样多组参数近似分布」的做法，可能可供核查能否廉价生成多假设以支持 LVR 中的答案验证、贡献分配或不确定性估计；但论文本身研究隐私攻击，未涉及推理状态，联系需较多核查。
